seo.title: Australia & Bali Semester Abroad | Pacific Discovery
seo.description: Australia & Bali in 10 weeks: canyoning in the Blue Mountains, surf camps, reef science on the Great Barrier Reef, K’gari, Bali’s rice terraces, a yoga retreat and a Mount Batur sunrise. Ages 17–22.

hero.headline: Australia’s east coast and Bali in one semester
hero.intro: Canyon in the Blue Mountains, learn to surf, survey the Great Barrier Reef and finish with Bali’s temples, rice fields and a sunrise on Mount Batur.

itinerary.heading: Week by week
itinerary.note: This is a guide to what you can expect to do on program. The order in which activities occur might vary. Itineraries are subject to change.

weeks.title: Sydney, surf life saving & permaculture
weeks.body:
You’ll meet your Program Instructors in Sydney and settle into Coogee for orientation, getting to know each other and taking a surf life saving session on the beach.

Then we head down the coast to Bermagui and The Crossing. Here we spend a permaculture design experience day, a Landcare day, and a bushfire prevention and wildlife tour at Potoroo Palace.
weeks.imageAlt: Turquoise bay below a coastal suburb

weeks.title: Forests, the capital & canyoning
weeks.body:
A forest regeneration day and an overnight hike wrap up our time in Bermagui. Next is Canberra, with a visit to Parliament, a city walking tour of the Parliamentary Triangle, Anzac Parade, the Australian War Memorial and Lake Burley Griffin, and a hike up Mt Ainslie.

In Katoomba we hike in the Blue Mountains straight from our accommodation, then spend a full day canyoning: hiking, scrambling, swimming and abseiling through an introductory canyon after learning abseiling skills.
weeks.imageAlt: Students standing in shallow water on a beach

weeks.title: Rainforest planting & learning to surf
weeks.body:
After a day exploring Sydney, we drive north to Crescent Head. Over three days of service with Maratus we plant trees on a property that holds 25% of the region’s remaining original rainforest, building tree guards, mulching and watering, and help a landowner remove invasive weeds.

We may also meet Aboriginal community members, learning to weave with lomandra grass and making clay sculptures and sand art from natural materials. Then the surf lessons start.

weeks.title: Surf, Byron Bay & Lamington
weeks.location: Crescent Head → Byron Bay → Stradbroke Island
weeks.body:
Three days of surf lessons with Crescent Surf get everyone riding waves. Then it’s on to Byron Bay to snorkel Julian Rocks (Nguthungulli), where tropical and temperate waters meet, with the chance to catch sunrise at Cape Byron Lighthouse and visit Nightcap National Park for waterfalls and glow worms.

From Binna Burra we hike in Lamington National Park, then take the ferry to Stradbroke Island.
weeks.imageAlt: Student sitting on coastal rocks above the sea

weeks.title: Straddie, K’gari & Australia Zoo
weeks.body:
On Stradbroke Island a First Nations tour takes us four-wheel driving, painting a boomerang to take home, along bush tracks and to morning tea at a billabong, followed by an afternoon of sandboarding.

From Noosa we cross to K’gari, the world’s largest sand island, staying at a beachfront eco retreat. We swim in freshwater lakes, walk inland tracks through towering forest and end the days with campfires and stargazing. Back on the mainland we spend a day at Australia Zoo.
weeks.imageAlt: Students on a zipline in the forest

weeks.title: Reef science on the Great Barrier Reef
weeks.body:
A walk in Noosa National Park, then we head to Brisbane and fly to Cairns.

Here we join Marine Discoveries for Reef Teach: an evening reef ecology seminar, then marine surveying days on Green Island and an outer reef pontoon, and a full day at Hastings Reef.
weeks.imageAlt: Group with gardening gloves and tools

weeks.title: Food rescue, mangroves & Balinese culture
weeks.body:
After a last day in Cairns, with Josephine Falls nearby, we fly to Bali. Following a rest and orientation day in Seminyak, we move to Sanur for two days with a food rescue organisation, helping prepare and distribute meals and visiting community programs including Bali Life Foundation.

A day of paddleboarding, mangrove restoration and rubbish removal comes with a snorkel. Then we head to Tabanan, where local guides introduce us to Balinese Hinduism, temples and traditional approaches to health and wellbeing.
weeks.imageAlt: Students walking along a path through green countryside

weeks.title: Rice terraces & Bali Starlings
weeks.body:
In Tabanan we trek through villages, rice terraces and farmland, join a morning of hands-on agriculture with local community members, and share dinner with members of the local royal family at Tabanan Palace.

Then we cross to Nusa Penida for three days with FNPF, protecting the critically endangered Bali Starling and supporting environmental restoration on the island, before a day to explore.
weeks.imageAlt: Group in traditional Balinese dress at a temple

weeks.title: Surf camp & spiritual Ubud
weeks.body:
Back on the mainland, a surf camp in Uluwatu with Balumba Surf builds skill, ocean awareness and confidence across several lessons, with a rest day to follow.

In Ubud we take in the evening markets and a show, then spend a full day with Five Pillars harvesting ingredients, preparing food, visiting temples and joining in ceremony. The week ends as our yoga retreat begins.
weeks.imageAlt: Group walking through a rice field

weeks.title: Yoga retreat, volcano sunrise & farewell
weeks.body:
Our yoga retreat focuses on yoga, meditation, mindfulness and personal wellbeing. Next we camp overnight on Mount Batur and climb to the summit for sunrise, then learn traditional batik, creating our own artwork with wax and dyes.

We finish in Kuta with our program wrap before flying home from Denpasar.
weeks.imageAlt: Group standing in front of a sea arch

notes.body: Medium activity level. Anyone with average fitness and enthusiasm for the outdoors will be fine. Expect hiking, canyoning, surfing and some physical work on volunteer projects.

safety.heading: For parents: how we keep students safe

items.title: 24/7 Emergency Line
items.body: Parents, students and instructors can reach a real person at any hour. Every call is logged and passed to our on-call staff member by phone.

items.title: Wilderness First Aid & Live Risk Assessment
items.body: All our instructors hold Wilderness First Aid (WFA) certification and have extensive training in group leadership and risk management.

items.title: Accredited Safety Systems
items.body: Our safety systems are assessed and accredited by the Gap Year Association (USA), Year Out Group (UK) and OutdoorsMark (NZ). Students on Go Overseas voted us one of the top gap year providers for safety.

items.title: Insurance & Health
items.body: Comprehensive travel insurance is required, covering medical costs and emergency evacuation. Check vaccinations with your doctor, and pack a first-aid kit and any personal medication. Our instructors can't legally give students any medication.

faq.heading: Questions we get about this program

items.q: Do I need to know how to surf?
items.a: No. Surf lessons start from the beginning at Crescent Head, and the surf camp in Uluwatu builds on what you learned.

items.q: How fit do I need to be?
items.a: The program suits anyone of average fitness. You don't need experience with any of the activities, but be ready to try hiking, canyoning, surfing and snorkeling. Volunteer projects also involve some physical work, such as tree planting and weeding.

Mostly clean, comfortable hostels and lodges, plus a campground stay at Crescent Head, an eco retreat on K’gari, the FNPF centre on Nusa Penida, a yoga retreat village in Ubud and a night camping on Mount Batur.
By group van in Australia, with a flight from Brisbane to Cairns and another from Cairns to Bali.

Tuition covers all in-country transport, accommodation, meals, and the activities and entry fees in the itinerary. It doesn't cover international flights, visas, travel insurance, spending money, optional college credit or optional activities.

items.q: How much spending money should I bring?
items.a: About $100 a week for snacks, laundry, personal shopping and optional activities. It varies from student to student.

items.q: Can I stay in touch with home?
items.a: Yes. We encourage keeping phones on flight mode so you stay present, and wifi is available where we stay in cities and towns. There will also be a photo album that students and instructors can upload photos and video to, so parents and caregivers can stay up to date.

items.q: Do I need a passport or visa?
items.a: Your passport must be valid for more than 6 months after the program ends. All the information you need in regard to visas will be available in your student portal.
